title: Tokengeist: Multi-Turn Attribution Tracing in Agentic Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2607.22610v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: When a model answers after several turns of dialogue and tool use, an overseer needs to know which earlier turns and intermediate steps it rests on. Attribution is the natural primitive for answering this, but existing context attribution methods process the full transcript in a single pass: they recover surface-level dependencies while missing the layered structure of multi-turn traces, in which an assistant turn is itself a derived artifact that condenses or transforms earlier context. translated_title: Tokengeist：智能体对话中的多轮归因追踪
translated_abstract: arXiv:2607.22610v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：当一个模型在经过多轮对话和工具使用后给出回答时，监督者需要了解该回答依赖于哪些较早的对话轮次和中间步骤。归因是回答这一问题的自然基础，但现有的上下文归因方法以单次处理方式处理完整对话记录：它们只能恢复表面层面的依赖关系，而遗漏了多轮追踪中的分层结构——在这种结构中，助手的某一轮回复本身就是一个派生产物，它对较早的上下文进行了压缩或转换。我们提出了多轮上下文归因（MTCA）：给定模型回复中的一个目标片段，该任务要求跨轮次向后追踪归因，不仅要识别哪些先前的轮次直接相关，还要识别这些轮次本身如何依赖于更早的上下文。我们提出了Tokengeist，一个与归因方法无关且可扩展的框架，它通过将归因转化为对有向无环图的递归遍历来恢复完整的依赖路径。
tldr: 该论文提出了多轮上下文归因（MTCA）任务以及Tokengeist框架，通过将有向无环图上的递归遍历作为归因方式来恢复完整依赖路径，解决了现有单次归因方法无法捕捉多轮对话分层依赖结构的问题。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces Multi-Turn Context Attribution (MTCA) and Tokengeist, a method-agnostic and scalable framework that recovers full dependency paths by casting attribution as recursive traversal of a directed acyclic graph, addressing the limitation of existing single-pass attribution methods that miss the layered structure of multi-turn conversations.
